plans.note: Section 9 is the primary liability clause; check mutuality of the cap, the cap amount relative to fees paid, and whether carve-outs (indemnity in sec-8-2, confidentiality in sec-10, willful misconduct) are excluded from the cap and from the consequential-damages waiver.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's third-party IP infringement indemnity covering the Software as hosted for our Customers; confirm defense/settlement control, no cap interaction, and that any Corio-side indemnity stays narrow.

Watch the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY constructs in the grant of rights, plus the sales/marketing cooperation exhibit, for limits on the markets we may serve or competing e-procurement products we may host or build.

Check whether the grant of rights or Exhibit D commits us to Commerce One as sole/preferred source of procurement software or requires us to lead with their product; we must retain freedom to license alternatives.

Pricing/revenue-sharing exhibit and fees section are where any 'best terms' language would sit; MFN running to us is acceptable, any obligation for us to give Commerce One our most favourable pricing or margins is not.
No dedicated non-solicit heading; if one appears in Miscellaneous or alongside confidentiality it must be mutual, ≤12 months and carve out general advertising and unsolicited applicants.

Section 11 governs term and termination; confirm we have termination on notice without penalty and that Commerce One cannot terminate mid-term other than for uncured material breach, given our downstream Customer commitments.
Look for automatic renewal terms and notice windows in Section 11, with any renewal fee escalation in the fees section or pricing exhibit; seek ≤30-60 day notice and capped uplift.

Governing law/venue and any dispute or arbitration mechanism (note the defined term RULES) should be in Miscellaneous; confirm California or another accepted jurisdiction and court venue rather than mandatory arbitration.

Assignment clause in Miscellaneous; we need affiliate/successor assignment without consent and must remove any Commerce One termination or consent right triggered by our change of control (check termination triggers in sec-11 too).

DEVELOPMENTS and EMPLOYEE NDA/INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions plus the grant of rights will allocate ownership; ensure our configurations, Customer data hosted on CORIO SERVERS and our service materials are not assigned to Commerce One.

Section 2 grant of rights read with the SOFTWARE/DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE/TERRITORY definitions and Exhibit A; the licence must be non-revocable during term and extend to our affiliates, subcontractors and hosting for Customers and Software Users.

Revenue-sharing reporting likely brings a records/audit right against us in the fees section or payment terms exhibit; limit to annually, on notice, during business hours, at Commerce One's cost absent material underpayment.
Check fees/payment terms for late-payment interest or penalty-style amounts payable by us; service credits or support remedies running in our favour (Exhibit C) are acceptable.

Section 7 warranties and disclaimer plus the Acceptance Test and Warranty Period definitions and delivery section; confirm a meaningful warranty duration, conformance to Documentation, and repair/replace/refund remedy backed by maintenance in sec-5 and Exhibit C.
No insurance heading appears; since Commerce One personnel support software hosting our Customers' data, propose a standard insurance covenant in Miscellaneous if none is buried near indemnification.

Fees section and pricing exhibit (including revenue sharing and IMPLEMENTATION FEE) are where minimum guarantees or committed volumes would appear; any minimum must be reducible or exitable on termination.

Effect-of-termination provisions in sec-11 plus the source code escrow in sec-12; we need wind-down rights for existing Customers, continued hosting during migration and return/retrieval of our and our Customers' data.
